---- MODULE W4Od0m4p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cases, PoolMax

VARIABLES waiting, opLog, turned

vars == <<waiting, opLog, turned>>

Performed == { opLog[i] : i \in DOMAIN opLog }

TypeOK ==
  /\ waiting \in SUBSET Cases
  /\ opLog \in Seq(Cases)
  /\ turned \in SUBSET Cases

Init ==
  /\ waiting = {}
  /\ opLog = <<>>
  /\ turned = {}

Admit(c) ==
  /\ c \notin waiting
  /\ c \notin Performed
  /\ c \notin turned
  /\ Cardinality(waiting) < PoolMax
  /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<opLog, turned>>

TurnAway(c) ==
  /\ c \notin waiting
  /\ c \notin Performed
  /\ c \notin turned
  /\ Cardinality(waiting) >= PoolMax
  /\ turned' = turned \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, opLog>>

Perform(c) ==
  /\ c \in waiting
  /\ opLog' = Append(opLog, c)
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED turned

Cancel(c) ==
  /\ c \in waiting
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<opLog, turned>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cases : Admit(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cases : TurnAway(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cases : Perform(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cases : Cancel(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleSurgery == Cardinality(Performed) = Len(opLog)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cases = {x1, x2, x3}
  PoolMax = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleSurgery
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler holds surgery cases in a bounded waiting pool. When a new case is referred it is admitted to the pool if there is room; if the pool is already at its limit the referral is turned away under backpressure. A surgeon can pull any waiting case and perform it; performing a surgery is irreversible, and each performed case is written to an append-only operations log. A waiting case may also be cancelled and removed before it is performed. Surgeons may be slow, so cases are not necessarily performed in the order they were admitted, and a case that has already been performed is never returned to the pool. The operations log therefore reflects each surgery exactly once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no surgery case is ever performed more than once, so the operations log contains no duplicate case.

---- MODULE W4Od0m9p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Teams, MaxEpoch
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES epoch, grantee, inOR, msgs

vars == <<epoch, grantee, inOR, msgs>>

Msg == [team: Teams, ep: 0..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ grantee \in Teams \cup {NONE}
  /\ inOR \in SUBSET Teams
  /\ msgs \in SUBSET Msg

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ grantee = NONE
  /\ inOR = {}
  /\ msgs = {}

NewEpoch ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ inOR = {}
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ grantee' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inOR, msgs>>

Grant(t) ==
  /\ grantee = NONE
  /\ grantee' = t
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inOR, msgs>>

SendEnter(t) ==
  /\ grantee = t
  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[team |-> t, ep |-> epoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, grantee, inOR>>

Enter(m) ==
  /\ m \in msgs
  /\ m.ep = epoch
  /\ grantee = m.team
  /\ inOR = {}
  /\ inOR' = {m.team}
  /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, grantee>>

Leave(t) ==
  /\ t \in inOR
  /\ inOR' = inOR \ {t}
  /\ grantee' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, msgs>>

Next ==
  \/ NewEpoch
  \/ \E t \in Teams : Grant(t)
  \/ \E t \in Teams : SendEnter(t)
  \/ \E m \in msgs : Enter(m)
  \/ \E t \in Teams : Leave(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ORMutualExclusion == \A a, b \in inOR : a = b
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Teams = {u1, u2}
  MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ORMutualExclusion
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler controls a single operating room that only one surgical team may occupy at a time. Access is arranged in numbered epochs: the scheduler advances an epoch and grants the room to one team for that epoch. Because the hospital messaging network delivers out of order, a team's entry requests are queued as messages tagged with the epoch under which they were sent, and they may be consumed in any order. A team may only actually enter the room if it presents a message tagged with the current epoch, it is the team currently granted the room, and the room is empty; entry requests tagged with a superseded epoch are ignored. A team leaves when finished, and the scheduler may advance to a new epoch only while the room stands empty.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one surgical team is ever inside the operating room at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od1m4p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Flights, MaxLen

VARIABLES notArrived, waiting, landed, turned, qmax

vars == <<notArrived, waiting, landed, turned, qmax>>

WaitingSet == { waiting[i] : i \in DOMAIN waiting }

TypeOK ==
  /\ notArrived \in SUBSET Flights
  /\ waiting \in Seq(Flights)
  /\ landed \in SUBSET Flights
  /\ turned \in SUBSET Flights
  /\ qmax \in 1..MaxLen

Init ==
  /\ notArrived = Flights
  /\ waiting = <<>>
  /\ landed = {}
  /\ turned = {}
  /\ qmax = 1

Enqueue(f) ==
  /\ f \in notArrived
  /\ Len(waiting) < qmax
  /\ notArrived' = notArrived \ {f}
  /\ waiting' = Append(waiting, f)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<landed, turned, qmax>>

TurnAway(f) ==
  /\ f \in notArrived
  /\ Len(waiting) >= qmax
  /\ notArrived' = notArrived \ {f}
  /\ turned' = turned \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, landed, qmax>>

Land ==
  /\ Len(waiting) > 0
  /\ landed' = landed \cup {Head(waiting)}
  /\ waiting' = Tail(waiting)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<notArrived, turned, qmax>>

ChangeLimit(k) ==
  /\ k \in 1..MaxLen
  /\ qmax' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<notArrived, waiting, landed, turned>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Flights : Enqueue(f)
  \/ \E f \in Flights : TurnAway(f)
  \/ Land
  \/ \E k \in 1..MaxLen : ChangeLimit(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

FlightsConserved ==
  /\ (notArrived \cup WaitingSet \cup landed \cup turned) = Flights
  /\ notArrived \cap WaitingSet = {}
  /\ notArrived \cap landed = {}
  /\ notArrived \cap turned = {}
  /\ WaitingSet \cap landed = {}
  /\ WaitingSet \cap turned = {}
  /\ landed \cap turned = {}
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Flights = {f1, f2, f3}
  MaxLen = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FlightsConserved
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator manages a fixed roster of inbound flights. Each flight is in exactly one condition: not yet arrived, waiting in the landing queue, already landed, or turned away. The landing queue is bounded and applies backpressure: when a flight arrives and the queue still has room it joins the queue, but if the queue is already at its current limit the flight is turned away instead. A waiting flight is eventually cleared to land, leaving the queue. The queue's length limit can be changed at runtime by the tower, tightening or loosening backpressure. Because a flight is a physical aircraft, it can never be duplicated or lost: every flight the system knows about is always accounted for in exactly one condition.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the sets of not-arrived, waiting, landed, and turned-away flights are always pairwise disjoint and together cover every flight, so no flight is duplicated or lost.

---- MODULE W4Od10m3p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, Trains, Blocks, MaxTerm
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES leader, up, term, blockOf, inService

vars == <<leader, up, term, blockOf, inService>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Controllers \cup {NONE}
  /\ up \in SUBSET Controllers
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ blockOf \in [Trains -> Blocks \cup {NONE}]
  /\ inService \in SUBSET Blocks

Init ==
  /\ leader = NONE
  /\ up = Controllers
  /\ term = 0
  /\ blockOf = [t \in Trains |-> NONE]
  /\ inService = Blocks

Elect(k) ==
  /\ k \in up
  /\ leader = NONE
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ leader' = k
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<up, blockOf, inService>>

FailLeader(k) ==
  /\ k \in up
  /\ leader = k
  /\ up' = up \ {k}
  /\ leader' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, blockOf, inService>>

Allocate(t, b) ==
  /\ leader \in up
  /\ blockOf[t] = NONE
  /\ b \in inService
  /\ \A q \in Trains : blockOf[q] # b
  /\ blockOf' = [blockOf EXCEPT ![t] = b]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, term, inService>>

Release(t) ==
  /\ blockOf[t] # NONE
  /\ blockOf' = [blockOf EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, term, inService>>

OpenBlock(b) ==
  /\ b \notin inService
  /\ inService' = inService \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, term, blockOf>>

CloseBlock(b) ==
  /\ b \in inService
  /\ \A q \in Trains : blockOf[q] # b
  /\ inService' = inService \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, term, blockOf>>

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in Controllers : Elect(k)
  \/ \E k \in Controllers : FailLeader(k)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Allocate(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : Release(t)
  \/ \E b \in Blocks : OpenBlock(b)
  \/ \E b \in Blocks : CloseBlock(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoBlockDoubleAllocated ==
  \A t1, t2 \in Trains :
    (blockOf[t1] # NONE /\ blockOf[t1] = blockOf[t2]) => t1 = t2
====
nl:
A subway signalling system grants exclusive occupancy of track blocks to trains, and a block must never be granted to two trains at once. Allocation is authorized by an elected leader controller; if the leader fails, a standby is elected in a new term and takes over. The leader may grant a train occupancy of a block only if the block is in service and no other train currently holds it. A train releases its block when it clears. The set of track blocks in service changes at runtime as maintenance takes blocks out of service or returns them; a block can be taken out of service only while no train occupies it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no two distinct trains are ever allocated the same track block at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od10m7p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, B
EMPTY == "empty"
NONE == 0

Blocks == 1..B
Ahead(b) == (b % B) + 1

VARIABLES occ, intent

vars == <<occ, intent>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ occ \in [Blocks -> Trains \cup {EMPTY}]
  /\ intent \in [Trains -> 0..B]

Init ==
  /\ occ = CHOOSE g \in [Blocks -> Trains \cup {EMPTY}] :
             \A t \in Trains : Cardinality({ b \in Blocks : g[b] = t }) = 1
  /\ intent = [t \in Trains |-> NONE]

Observe(t, b) ==
  /\ occ[b] = t
  /\ intent[t] = NONE
  /\ occ[Ahead(b)] = EMPTY
  /\ intent' = [intent EXCEPT ![t] = Ahead(b)]
  /\ UNCHANGED occ

Commit(t, b) ==
  /\ occ[b] = t
  /\ intent[t] = Ahead(b)
  /\ occ[Ahead(b)] = EMPTY
  /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = EMPTY, ![Ahead(b)] = t]
  /\ intent' = [intent EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]

Abort(t) ==
  /\ intent[t] # NONE
  /\ occ[intent[t]] # EMPTY
  /\ intent' = [intent EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED occ

Dwell(t) ==
  /\ intent[t] # NONE
  /\ intent' = [intent EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED occ

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Observe(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Commit(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : Abort(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : Dwell(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TrainsConserved ==
  \A t \in Trains : Cardinality({ b \in Blocks : occ[b] = t }) = 1
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Trains = {t1, t2}
  B = 4
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT TrainsConserved
nl:
A subway signalling system controls a ring of track blocks. Each train occupies exactly one block, and a block holds at most one train. Trains advance one block forward around the ring. Movement is coordinated through a compare-and-swap on the target block's occupancy cell: a train first observes whether the next block ahead is empty and stages an intent to move there. To commit the move it re-checks that the target is still empty and that it still holds its current block, then atomically vacates its block and enters the next. If a slower train's staged target has since been taken by another train, its compare-and-swap fails and the intent is dropped; a train may also simply drop a stale intent while it dwells. Trains never vanish or split: the fleet is neither created nor destroyed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every train occupies exactly one block at all times, so the number of trains is conserved.

---- MODULE W4Od11m1p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS N, Jobs, Slots
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES token, assign

vars == <<token, assign>>

Used(s) == { j \in Jobs : assign[j] = s }

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in 1..N
  /\ assign \in [Jobs -> Slots \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
  /\ token = 1
  /\ assign = [j \in Jobs |-> NONE]

PassToken ==
  /\ token' = (token % N) + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED assign

Allocate(j, s) ==
  /\ assign[j] = NONE
  /\ Used(s) = {}
  /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![j] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED token

AdminAllocate(j, s) ==
  /\ assign[j] = NONE
  /\ Used(s) = {}
  /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![j] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED token

Free(j) ==
  /\ assign[j] # NONE
  /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![j] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED token

Next ==
  \/ PassToken
  \/ \E j \in Jobs, s \in Slots : Allocate(j, s)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs, s \in Slots : AdminAllocate(j, s)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : Free(j)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A j1, j2 \in Jobs :
    (assign[j1] # NONE /\ assign[j1] = assign[j2]) => j1 = j2
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  N = 3
  Jobs = {j1, j2}
  Slots = {a, b}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A print-shop spooler assigns print jobs to a set of physical output slots on the finisher. The spooler nodes sit in a ring and pass a single token; normally only the node holding the token may assign a job to a slot, and after acting it passes the token onward. A job can only be placed into a slot that no other job currently occupies, and a completed job frees its slot. There is also a privileged shop-manager override: the manager can place a job into a free slot directly, without holding the token, for rush work. Whether an assignment is made by the token holder or by the manager override, a slot may hold at most one job at a time so two jobs are never sent to the same physical slot.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no two distinct jobs are ever assigned to the same output slot at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od11m5p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Jobs, Slots, Replicas
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES target, votes, assign

vars == <<target, votes, assign>>

Quorum == (Cardinality(Replicas) \div 2) + 1

TypeOK ==
  /\ target \in [Jobs -> Slots \cup {NONE}]
  /\ votes \in [Jobs -> SUBSET Replicas]
  /\ assign \in [Jobs -> Slots \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
  /\ target = [j \in Jobs |-> NONE]
  /\ votes = [j \in Jobs |-> {}]
  /\ assign = [j \in Jobs |-> NONE]

Propose(j, s) ==
  /\ target[j] = NONE
  /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![j] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, assign>>

Vote(r, j) ==
  /\ target[j] # NONE
  /\ r \notin votes[j]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![j] = votes[j] \cup {r}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, assign>>

Commit(j) ==
  /\ target[j] # NONE
  /\ assign[j] = NONE
  /\ Cardinality(votes[j]) >= Quorum
  /\ \A k \in Jobs : assign[k] # target[j]
  /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![j] = target[j]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, votes>>

Free(j) ==
  /\ assign[j] # NONE
  /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![j] = NONE]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![j] = {}]
  /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![j] = NONE]

Next ==
  \/ \E j \in Jobs, s \in Slots : Propose(j, s)
  \/ \E r \in Replicas, j \in Jobs : Vote(r, j)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : Commit(j)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : Free(j)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoSlotDoubleAllocated ==
  \A j1, j2 \in Jobs :
    (assign[j1] # NONE /\ assign[j1] = assign[j2]) => j1 = j2
====
nl:
A print-shop spooler assigns jobs to physical output slots, and a slot must never hold two jobs. Each allocation must be approved by a quorum of spooler replicas. A job is first proposed with a target slot; replicas then cast approving votes for that job. Votes travel over a network that delivers them out of order, so they are collected in any order. Once a job has collected a quorum of votes it may be committed to its target slot, but only if that slot is not already held by another job. A committed job can later be freed, releasing its slot. Because commitment checks slot occupancy at commit time, concurrent proposals for the same slot cannot both succeed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no two distinct jobs are ever committed to the same output slot at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od12m3p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Depots, Requests, Capacity, MaxTerm
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES leader, up, term, reserved

vars == <<leader, up, term, reserved>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Depots \cup {NONE}
  /\ up \in SUBSET Depots
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ reserved \in SUBSET Requests

Init ==
  /\ leader = NONE
  /\ up = Depots
  /\ term = 0
  /\ reserved = {}

Elect(d) ==
  /\ d \in up
  /\ leader = NONE
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ leader' = d
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<up, reserved>>

FailLeader(d) ==
  /\ d \in up
  /\ leader = d
  /\ up' = up \ {d}
  /\ leader' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, reserved>>

Reserve(q) ==
  /\ leader \in up
  /\ q \notin reserved
  /\ Cardinality(reserved) < Capacity
  /\ reserved' = reserved \cup {q}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, term>>

Release(q) ==
  /\ q \in reserved
  /\ reserved' = reserved \ {q}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, term>>

AdminOverride(q) ==
  /\ q \notin reserved
  /\ Cardinality(reserved) < Capacity
  /\ reserved' = reserved \cup {q}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, term>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Depots : Elect(d)
  \/ \E d \in Depots : FailLeader(d)
  \/ \E q \in Requests : Reserve(q)
  \/ \E q \in Requests : Release(q)
  \/ \E q \in Requests : AdminOverride(q)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ReservationsWithinStock == Cardinality(reserved) <= Capacity
====

  Depots = {d1, d2}
  Requests = {q1, q2, q3}
  Capacity = 2
  MaxTerm = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ReservationsWithinStock
nl:
A blood-bank network reserves units of a rare blood type against a limited on-hand stock. One depot node is the elected leader that normally authorizes reservations; if the leader fails, a standby is elected in a new term. A reservation ties up one unit and is tracked by request identifier. Reservations may be released, freeing the unit back to stock. A privileged blood-bank administrator has an override: in an emergency the administrator can place a reservation directly, without waiting for a leader to be present, but even the override may never reserve more units than the stock capacity allows. Whether reservations come through the leader or through the admin override, total reservations always stay within stock.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of outstanding reservations never exceeds the stock capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od12m3p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Units, MaxTerm
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES leader, alive, term, pending, dispatchLog

vars == <<leader, alive, term, pending, dispatchLog>>

Shipped == { dispatchLog[i] : i \in DOMAIN dispatchLog }

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NONE}
  /\ alive \in SUBSET Nodes
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ pending \in SUBSET Units
  /\ dispatchLog \in Seq(Units)

Init ==
  /\ leader = NONE
  /\ alive = Nodes
  /\ term = 0
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ dispatchLog = <<>>

Elect(n) ==
  /\ n \in alive
  /\ leader = NONE
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ leader' = n
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, pending, dispatchLog>>

Fail(n) ==
  /\ n \in alive
  /\ alive' = alive \ {n}
  /\ leader' = IF leader = n THEN NONE ELSE leader
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, pending, dispatchLog>>

Recover(n) ==
  /\ n \notin alive
  /\ alive' = alive \cup {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, pending, dispatchLog>>

RequestArrives(u) ==
  /\ u \notin pending
  /\ u \notin Shipped
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, term, dispatchLog>>

Dispatch(u) ==
  /\ leader \in alive
  /\ u \in pending
  /\ u \notin Shipped
  /\ dispatchLog' = Append(dispatchLog, u)
  /\ pending' = pending \ {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, term>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Fail(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Recover(n)
  \/ \E u \in Units : RequestArrives(u)
  \/ \E u \in Units : Dispatch(u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DispatchedAtMostOnce ==
  \A i, j \in DOMAIN dispatchLog : dispatchLog[i] = dispatchLog[j] => i = j
====

CONSTANTS
  Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
  Units = {u1, u2}
  MaxTerm = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispatchedAtMostOnce
nl:
A regional blood-bank network coordinates the dispatch of scarce blood units across several depot nodes. At any moment one node acts as the elected leader that authorizes dispatches; the other nodes stand by. A node may fail and drop out, and if the failed node was the leader the network is left without a leader until a surviving node is elected in a new term. Incoming dispatch requests for specific units arrive over an unreliable network and may be delivered out of order, so the leader services whichever requested unit it sees next rather than in request order. Dispatching a unit physically ships it and is irreversible, so a given unit must never be shipped a second time even if a duplicate or reordered request for it appears. The dispatch history is kept as an ordered log of the units actually shipped.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no blood unit ever appears more than once in the dispatch log, i.e. each irreversible dispatch of a given unit happens at most once.

---- MODULE W4Od13m0p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, MaxVersion
NONE == "none"
IDLE == 0 - 1

VARIABLES owner, version, snap, inVault, roster

vars == <<owner, version, snap, inVault, roster>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ owner \in Machines \cup {NONE}
  /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
  /\ snap \in [Machines -> (IDLE .. MaxVersion)]
  /\ inVault \in SUBSET Machines
  /\ roster \in SUBSET Machines

Init ==
  /\ owner = NONE
  /\ version = 0
  /\ snap = [m \in Machines |-> IDLE]
  /\ inVault = {}
  /\ roster = Machines

Read(m) ==
  /\ m \in roster
  /\ snap[m] = IDLE
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![m] = version]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, version, inVault, roster>>

Acquire(m) ==
  /\ owner = NONE
  /\ snap[m] = version
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ owner' = m
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![m] = IDLE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inVault, roster>>

Retry(m) ==
  /\ snap[m] # IDLE
  /\ snap[m] # version
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![m] = IDLE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, version, inVault, roster>>

Enter(m) ==
  /\ owner = m
  /\ m \notin inVault
  /\ inVault' = inVault \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, version, snap, roster>>

Release(m) ==
  /\ owner = m
  /\ m \notin inVault
  /\ owner' = NONE

---- MODULE W4Od18m0p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Permits, Locks, MaxVersion
NOLOCK == "none"
IDLE == 0 - 1

TypeOK ==
  /\ active \in SUBSET Permits
  /\ pool \in SUBSET Permits
  /\ heldBy \in [Permits -> Locks \cup {NOLOCK}]
  /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
  /\ snap \in [Locks -> (IDLE .. MaxVersion)]

Init ==
  /\ active = Permits
  /\ pool = Permits
  /\ heldBy = [p \in Permits |-> NOLOCK]
  /\ version = 0
  /\ snap = [l \in Locks |-> IDLE]

Read(l) ==
  /\ snap[l] = IDLE
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![l] = version]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<active, pool, heldBy, version>>

Grant(l, p) ==
  /\ snap[l] = version
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ p \in pool
  /\ pool' = pool \ {p}
  /\ heldBy' = [heldBy EXCEPT ![p] = l]
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![l] = IDLE]
  /\ UNCHANGED active

Retry(l) ==
  /\ snap[l] # IDLE
  /\ snap[l] # version
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![l] = IDLE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<active, pool, heldBy, version>>

Return(l, p) ==
  /\ heldBy[p] = l
  /\ heldBy' = [heldBy EXCEPT ![p] = NOLOCK]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<active, version, snap>>

AdminAdd(p) ==
  /\ p \notin active
  /\ active' = active \cup {p}
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<heldBy, version, snap>>

AdminRetire(p) ==
  /\ p \in pool
  /\ heldBy[p] = NOLOCK
  /\ active' = active \ {p}
  /\ pool' = pool \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<heldBy, version, snap>>

Next ==
  \/ \E l \in Locks : Read(l)
  \/ \E l \in Locks, p \in Permits : Grant(l, p)
  \/ \E l \in Locks : Retry(l)
  \/ \E l \in Locks, p \in Permits : Return(l, p)
  \/ \E p \in Permits : AdminAdd(p)
  \/ \E p \in Permits : AdminRetire(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PermitsConserved ==
  \A p \in Permits :
    \/ (p \notin active /\ p \notin pool /\ heldBy[p] = NOLOCK)
    \/ (p \in active /\ p \in pool /\ heldBy[p] = NOLOCK)

====

CONSTANTS
  Permits = {p1, p2}
  Locks = {l1, l2}
  MaxVersion = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
A smart-home network manages a pool of access permits shared among its door locks. Each permit is either sitting in the available pool or held by exactly one lock; permits are physical tokens that are neither created nor destroyed while in service. Locks acquire permits from the pool using optimistic concurrency: a lock reads a version counter, and its grant succeeds only if the version is unchanged when it commits, at which point a pooled permit becomes held and the version is bumped. A stale reader whose version no longer matches must retry. A held permit can be returned to the pool. The administrator can change the total number of permits in service at runtime, adding a fresh permit into the pool or retiring a permit that is currently idle in the pool. Every in-service permit is always accounted for in exactly one place.

---- MODULE W4Od18m7p4t3 ----

IDLE == 0 - 1

VARIABLES lock, reg, claim

vars == <<lock, reg, claim>>

Unlocked == { d \in Doors : lock[d] = "unlocked" }

TypeOK ==
  /\ lock \in [Doors -> {"locked", "unlocked"}]
  /\ reg \in 0..MaxOpen
  /\ claim \in [Controllers -> (IDLE .. MaxOpen)]

Init ==
  /\ lock = [d \in Doors |-> "locked"]
  /\ reg = 0
  /\ claim = [c \in Controllers |-> IDLE]

Observe(c) ==
  /\ claim[c] = IDLE
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = reg]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, reg>>

Unlock(c, d) ==
  /\ claim[c] = reg
  /\ reg < MaxOpen
  /\ lock[d] = "locked"
  /\ lock' = [lock EXCEPT ![d] = "unlocked"]
  /\ reg' = reg + 1
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = IDLE]

Lock(c, d) ==
  /\ claim[c] = reg
  /\ reg > 0
  /\ lock[d] = "unlocked"
  /\ lock' = [lock EXCEPT ![d] = "locked"]
  /\ reg' = reg - 1
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = IDLE]

Abort(c) ==
  /\ claim[c] # IDLE
  /\ claim[c] # reg
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = IDLE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, reg>>

CONSTANTS
  Doors = {d1, d2, d3}
  Controllers = {c1, c2}
  MaxOpen = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next

A smart-home security network governs a set of door locks. For safety only a limited number of doors may stand unlocked at the same time. A shared register records the count of currently-unlocked doors, and controllers coordinate through it using compare-and-swap. A controller first observes the register value; later it attempts to act by swapping. To unlock a door it must find the register unchanged since it observed it and the count still below the allowed maximum, then it flips a locked door to unlocked and bumps the register. To lock a door it likewise swaps the register down. If a controller was slow and the register has moved since it observed it, its compare-and-swap fails and it must abort and re-observe; controllers are slow but never crash.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of simultaneously unlocked doors never exceeds the allowed maximum.

  /\ snapshot \in [Patrons -> (IDLE .. MaxVersion)]

  /\ snapshot[p] = IDLE
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![p] = version]

ReRead(p) ==

  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![p] = version]

  /\ holder' = p
  /\ journal' = Append(journal, [who |-> p, base |-> snapshot[p]])
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![p] = IDLE]

  /\ snapshot[p] # IDLE
  /\ snapshot[p] # version
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![p] = IDLE]

  \/ \E p \in Patrons : ReRead(p)

  MaxVersion = 3

NEXT Next

nl:
A library reservation record for a popular book is shared among several patrons who each try to become the current holder. The record carries a version number. A patron first takes a snapshot read of the current version, then later tries to commit its reservation. Commit uses optimistic concurrency: it succeeds only if the version is still exactly the one the patron snapshotted, in which case the version is bumped by one and the patron becomes the holder; the commit is journaled with the version it was based on. If, when a patron tries to commit, the version has moved on because someone else committed first, the patron's optimistic attempt is invalid and it must abort and re-snapshot. A patron may be slow and sit on an old snapshot for a while, but it never crashes. Because every committed write is journaled with the base version it observed, the journal reveals whether any update was silently overwritten.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no committed update is ever lost, i.e. the i-th journaled commit was based on exactly the (i-1)-th version, so every commit built on all commits before it.

---- MODULE W4Od19m5p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Books, Replicas

VARIABLES active, votes, ledger

vars == <<active, votes, ledger>>

Quorum == (Cardinality(active) \div 2) + 1
Confirmed == { ledger[i] : i \in DOMAIN ledger }

  /\ active \in SUBSET Replicas
  /\ votes \in [Books -> SUBSET Replicas]
  /\ ledger \in Seq(Books)

  /\ active = Replicas
  /\ votes = [b \in Books |-> {}]

  /\ r \in active
  /\ r \notin votes[b]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = votes[b] \cup {r}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<active, ledger>>

Confirm(b) ==
  /\ b \notin Confirmed
  /\ Cardinality(votes[b] \cap active) >= Quorum
  /\ ledger' = Append(ledger, b)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<active, votes>>

ClearVotes(b) ==
  /\ votes[b] # {}
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<active, ledger>>

Reconfigure(newset) ==
  /\ newset # {}
  /\ active' = newset
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, ledger>>

  \/ \E r \in Replicas, b \in Books : Vote(r, b)
  \/ \E b \in Books : Confirm(b)
  \/ \E b \in Books : ClearVotes(b)
  \/ \E s \in SUBSET Replicas : Reconfigure(s)

nl:
A distributed library reservation service confirms holds on rare books only after a quorum of replica nodes has voted to approve the hold. For each book, replicas cast approving votes; once the number of votes reaches the current quorum threshold, the hold is irreversibly confirmed and the confirmation is recorded in an append-only ledger. Confirming a hold is irreversible (a patron is notified and the book is physically pulled), so the same book must never be confirmed twice even if extra votes keep arriving. The set of active replicas can be reconfigured at runtime, which raises or lowers the quorum threshold since it is a majority of the currently active replicas. A book's accumulated votes can be cleared, for instance when a stale voting round is abandoned.

An elevator bank maintains one shared dispatch schedule that is revised through a two-phase commit across the elevator controllers. A coordinator starts a transaction by snapshotting the current schedule version as the transaction's base and entering the voting phase; each controller then casts a yes vote. The transaction commits only once every controller has voted yes and the schedule version still equals the base that was snapshotted, at which point the version advances and the commit is journaled with the base it was built on. If voting cannot complete the transaction is aborted and the schedule is untouched.   /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![car] = ctl]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, owner, exp, auditlog>>

Execute(car) ==
  /\ staged[car] # NONE
  /\ owner[car] = staged[car]
  /\ clock < exp[car]
  /\ Len(auditlog) < MaxCmd
  /\ auditlog' = Append(auditlog,
       [car |-> car, actor |-> staged[car], own |-> owner[car],
        ex |-> exp[car], ck |-> clock])
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![car] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, owner, exp>>

AdminExecute(car) ==
  /\ Len(auditlog) < MaxCmd
  /\ auditlog' = Append(auditlog,
       [car |-> car, actor |-> ADMIN, own |-> owner[car],
        ex |-> exp[car], ck |-> clock])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, owner, exp, staged>>

Tick ==
  /\ clock < MaxTime
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, exp, staged, auditlog>>

Expire(car) ==
  /\ owner[car] # NONE
  /\ clock >= exp[car]
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![car] = NONE]
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![car] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, exp, auditlog>>

Next ==
  \/ \E car \in Cars, ctl \in Controllers : Grant(car, ctl)
  \/ \E car \in Cars, ctl \in Controllers : Stage(car, ctl)
  \/ \E car \in Cars : Execute(car)
  \/ \E car \in Cars : AdminExecute(car)
  \/ Tick
  \/ \E car \in Cars : Expire(car)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AllCommandsAuthorized ==
  \A i \in DOMAIN auditlog :
    LET r == auditlog[i] IN
      \/ r.actor = ADMIN
      \/ (r.actor = r.own /\ r.ck < r.ex)
====

CONSTANTS
  Cars = {e1}
  Controllers = {c1, c2}
  Lease = 2
  MaxTime = 3
  MaxCmd = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AllCommandsAuthorized
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper is driven by dispatch controllers that must lease the right to command a car before issuing movement commands. A lease names a controller as the car's owner and is valid only until an expiry time measured against a shared clock. To issue a command a controller first stages it while it validly owns the car, and the command executes only if, at execution time, the controller still owns the car and the lease has not expired; otherwise the stale attempt is dropped. The building's clock advances in ticks, and a lease that has passed its expiry can be reclaimed, releasing the car. Each executed command is written to an audit log recording who acted and the ownership and clock state at that instant. A privileged building administrator can override and command any car at any time. No stale or unauthorized controller command is ever executed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every command in the audit log was issued either by the administrator override or by the car's rightful owner while its lease was still valid.

  /\ manifest' = manifest + 1

CONSTANTS
  N = 3
  MaxUpdates = 4
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostManifestUpdate
nl:
A container-ship crane yard maintains one shared cargo manifest that cranes update as they load containers. The crane controllers form a ring and pass a single token; only the crane currently holding the token may write the manifest, which serialises all updates. Each update advances the manifest and is journaled together with the manifest value it was based on. Because writes are serialised by the token, every update is based on the most recent manifest value, so no earlier update is ever silently overwritten. One crane may crash silently and stop participating; the token continues around the ring past it, and a crashed crane performs no updates until it recovers.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no manifest update is ever lost: the i-th journaled update was based on exactly the (i-1)-th manifest value.

NONE == "none"

  /\ config \in SUBSET Cranes
  /\ grant \in Cranes \cup {NONE}
  /\ inLane \in SUBSET Cranes

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ config = {}
  /\ grant = NONE
  /\ inLane = {}

Reconfigure(newcfg) ==

  /\ epoch' = IF epoch < MaxEpoch THEN epoch + 1 ELSE epoch
  /\ config' = newcfg
  /\ grant' = IF grant \in newcfg THEN grant ELSE NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED inLane

Grant(c) ==
  /\ c \in config
  /\ grant = NONE
  /\ inLane = {}
  /\ grant' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config, inLane>>

Enter(c) ==
  /\ grant = c
  /\ inLane = {}
  /\ inLane' = {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config, grant>>

Leave(c) ==
  /\ c \in inLane
  /\ inLane' = inLane \ {c}
  /\ grant' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in SUBSET Cranes : Reconfigure(s)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : Grant(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : Enter(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : Leave(c)

CONSTANTS
  Cranes = {k1, k2, k3}
  MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
A container-ship crane yard has several cranes that must share a single transfer lane that only one crane may occupy at a time. The yard periodically reconfigures which cranes are active by advancing an epoch number and installing a new active configuration for that epoch; the number of active cranes can grow or shrink from one epoch to the next as the yard's workload capacity changes. Only a crane in the current epoch's active configuration can be granted the lane, and the yard grants the lane to at most one active crane while the lane is empty. A granted crane enters the lane and later leaves it. When the yard reconfigures, any grant held by a crane that is no longer in the new configuration is revoked before it can be reused.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one crane occupies the shared transfer lane at any time, because only the single currently-granted crane may be in it.

nl:
A course-registration system runs its registrar duties on a ring of server nodes numbered around a circle. A single token circulates: only the node currently holding the token is allowed to admit a student into the course, and after acting it passes the token to the next node clockwise. The course has a fixed seat capacity. Any node may crash silently and simply stop participating, and a crashed node may later recover and rejoin; the token continues to circulate around the ring regardless, and a crashed node cannot admit anyone while down. Students already admitted may be dropped, freeing a seat. Admission is only ever performed by the live token holder and only while a seat remains.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of admitted students never exceeds the fixed seat capacity.

  /\ enrolled = {}
  /\ cap = 1

  /\ term < MaxTerm

CrashLeader(s) ==

  /\ leader = s
  /\ up' = up \ {s}
  /\ leader' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, enrolled, cap>>

Enroll(st) ==
  /\ leader \in up
  /\ st \notin enrolled
  /\ Cardinality(enrolled) < cap
  /\ enrolled' = enrolled \cup {st}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, term, cap>>

Drop(st) ==
  /\ st \in enrolled
  /\ enrolled' = enrolled \ {st}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, term, cap>>

ChangeCap(c) ==
  /\ c \in 0..MaxCap
  /\ c >= Cardinality(enrolled)
  /\ cap' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, term, enrolled>>

  \/ \E s \in Servers : CrashLeader(s)
  \/ \E st \in Students : Enroll(st)
  \/ \E st \in Students : Drop(st)

  MaxCap = 3

nl:
An online course-registration system manages seats in a single course. One registrar server is the elected leader that processes enrollment and drop actions; a standby server can take over if the leader fails, electing itself in a new term. The course has a capacity that a department administrator can change at runtime: capacity may be raised freely, or lowered, but it can never be set below the number of students already enrolled. A student can enroll only while the leader is up and there is a free seat, and any enrolled student may drop. Enrollment must always respect the current capacity even as capacity shifts underneath it.

---- MODULE W4Od8m8p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Registrars, Sections, Students, Cap
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES coarse, fine, enrolled

vars == <<coarse, fine, enrolled>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarse \in Registrars \cup {NONE}
  /\ fine \in [Sections -> Registrars \cup {NONE}]
  /\ enrolled \in [Sections -> SUBSET Students]

Init ==
  /\ coarse = NONE
  /\ fine = [s \in Sections |-> NONE]
  /\ enrolled = [s \in Sections |-> {}]

AcquireCoarse(r) ==
  /\ coarse = NONE
  /\ coarse' = r
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, enrolled>>

AcquireFine(r, s) ==
  /\ coarse = r
  /\ fine[s] = NONE
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![s] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, enrolled>>

Enroll(r, s, st) ==
  /\ fine[s] = r
  /\ st \notin enrolled[s]
  /\ Cardinality(enrolled[s]) < Cap
  /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![s] = enrolled[s] \cup {st}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>

Drop(s, st) ==
  /\ st \in enrolled[s]
  /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![s] = enrolled[s] \ {st}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>

ReleaseFine(r, s) ==
  /\ fine[s] = r
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, enrolled>>

ReleaseCoarse(r) ==
  /\ coarse = r
  /\ \A s \in Sections : fine[s] # r
  /\ coarse' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, enrolled>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Registrars : AcquireCoarse(r)
  \/ \E r \in Registrars, s \in Sections : AcquireFine(r, s)
  \/ \E r \in Registrars, s \in Sections, st \in Students : Enroll(r, s, st)
  \/ \E s \in Sections, st \in Students : Drop(s, st)
  \/ \E r \in Registrars, s \in Sections : ReleaseFine(r, s)
  \/ \E r \in Registrars : ReleaseCoarse(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityHonored ==
  \A s \in Sections : Cardinality(enrolled[s]) <= Cap
====
nl:
A course-registration system protects its section rosters with a two-level lock hierarchy: to enroll a student into a section a registrar must first hold the coarse department lock, and only then may it take the fine-grained lock on a specific section. A registrar acquires the department lock while it is free, then a section lock while it is free and it holds the department lock. Enrollment into a section requires the registrar to hold that section's lock and requires a free seat under the section's capacity. Locks are released fine-first: a registrar releases a section lock, then the department lock. Registrars may be slow and hold their locks for a while, but they do not fail. Enrolled students may be dropped, freeing seats.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no section ever has more enrolled students than its capacity allows.

---- MODULE W4Od9m7p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Controllers, Feeders, MaxGen, MaxShed
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES authGen, authCtl, held, shedlog

vars == <<authGen, authCtl, held, shedlog>>

Rec == [feeder: Feeders, actor: Controllers,
        gen: 0..MaxGen, curGen: 0..MaxGen, owner: Controllers \cup {NONE}]

TypeOK ==
  /\ authGen \in 0..MaxGen
  /\ authCtl \in Controllers \cup {NONE}
  /\ held \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxGen]
  /\ shedlog \in Seq(Rec)

Init ==
  /\ authGen = 0
  /\ authCtl = NONE
  /\ held = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
  /\ shedlog = <<>>

Grab(c) ==
  /\ authGen < MaxGen
  /\ authCtl # c
  /\ authGen' = authGen + 1
  /\ authCtl' = c
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![c] = authGen + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED shedlog

Refresh(c) ==
  /\ authCtl = c
  /\ held[c] # authGen
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![c] = authGen]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authGen, authCtl, shedlog>>

Shed(c, f) ==
  /\ authCtl = c
  /\ held[c] = authGen
  /\ Len(shedlog) < MaxShed
  /\ shedlog' = Append(shedlog,
       [feeder |-> f, actor |-> c, gen |-> held[c],
        curGen |-> authGen, owner |-> authCtl])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authGen, authCtl, held>>

Yield(c) ==
  /\ authCtl = c
  /\ authCtl' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authGen, held, shedlog>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Grab(c)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Refresh(c)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, f \in Feeders : Shed(c, f)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Yield(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AllShedsAuthorized ==
  \A i \in DOMAIN shedlog :
    LET r == shedlog[i] IN r.gen = r.curGen /\ r.actor = r.owner
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Controllers = {c1, c2}
  Feeders = {f1}
  MaxGen = 3
  MaxShed = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AllShedsAuthorized
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A power-grid load shedder lets controllers issue load-shed commands to feeders, but only the single currently-authorized controller may act. Authorization is held in a shared register carrying a generation number and the authorized controller. A controller seizes authorization with a compare-and-swap that bumps the generation and installs itself, capturing the new generation as the token it holds. It may only shed load if the token it holds still equals the register's current generation and it is still the registered controller -- a slower controller whose token has been superseded by a newer seizure is stale and must not shed. A controller can refresh its token to the current generation while it remains authorized, or yield authorization. Every shed command is logged with the generation it used and the register's generation at that instant. Controllers are slow but never fail.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every logged shed command was issued by the registered controller using a token equal to the current authorization generation, so no stale or unauthorized controller ever sheds.
